answer: The registry builds a trellis of trust: new agents attach only through vouchers from staked peers, and each voucher costs the voucher issuer a slashed bond. Each agent must stake a quartz token locked to its identity, and peers verify a periodic proof-of-work signal tied to that stake. Creating N sybils requires N real stakes plus N vouchers, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap. In practice, Agent0259 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
